name: issue-first-wireframe-attention-profile
purpose: Prioritize issue comprehension and action in the first viewport while preserving scroll continuation and progressive disclosure.

research_basis.title: Scrolling and Attention
research_basis.author: Therese Fessenden
research_basis.reported_sample: 120 participants; 130,000+ eye fixations across varied websites/tasks
research_basis.caveat: These are aggregate viewing-time observations, not a guaranteed per-user conversion curve and not a fixed pixel law.

research_basis.title: Web page visual hierarchy: Examining Faraday's guidelines for entry points
research_basis.finding: Spatial position, color, and text style predicted earlier attention better than size alone.

research_basis.title: How do we react to cluttered displays? Evidence from the first seconds of visual search in websites
research_basis.finding: High-clutter websites produced a wider spread of attention during the first 3 seconds of visual search.

research_basis.title: Web pages: What can you see in a single fixation?
research_basis.finding: Observers could classify page category and infer spatial layout above chance after a 120 ms fixation.

research_basis.title: The Effects of Layout Order on Interface Complexity: An Eye-Tracking Study for Dashboard Design
research_basis.finding: Layout order affects search behavior; placing the core chart in a left-centered position improved visual search in the studied dashboard conditions.

attention_budget.interpretation: Use as a prioritization prior for vertical information architecture, not as a prediction of exact user behavior.

bands.share_semantics: aggregate across all remaining page depth; not 19% per screen

first_screen_internal_rule.top_half: Reserve the strongest visual hierarchy for the issue capsule and primary action. Research summary reports >65% of first-screen viewing time in the top half.
first_screen_internal_rule.bottom_half: Use for compact evidence/impact preview and a visible continuation cue; do not create a false floor.

mobile.priority: issue capsule must be visible before nonessential chrome/content
mobile.continuation_cue: show that more evidence/detail exists below without crowding the first viewport

desktop.priority: place issue capsule in the spatial entry region and logical-start reading path; do not rely on size alone
desktop.side_panel_rule: secondary history/reference may use side panels only if they do not compete with the issue capsule

wireframe_validation.target_principle: Users should be able to state the issue, its current status, and the next action without scrolling.
